 W.P.(C)Nos.13743 - P and
 15413 of 2017 - B
 =========================
 Dated this the 13th day of July, 2017
 J U D G M E N T

The issue raised in the above writ petition is with respect to a restaurant carried on in the name of New Malabar Restaurant in a property originally owned by one Jessy Joseph; in Survey No.95/17A comprised in Edapally North Village, in building No.49/1598 C.
2. W.P.(C) No.13743 of 2017 was filed by the petitioner therein seeking a direction to the Corporation to verify as to whether the 3rd respondent is carrying on the restaurant with a D&O license and license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and if not to stop the restaurant forthwith.

An interim order dated 28.04.2017 was passed directing verification of whether the 3rd respondent is carrying on the & 15413/2017 activity with proper permits and licenses from the respective statutory authorities.
The 3rd respondent was then directed by the Corporation to stop the activity orally and the premises was locked and key taken over by the Corporation.
The 3rd respondent challenged such action before this Court by W.P. (C) No.15413 of 2017, from which the documents and parties are referred to.
3. The petitioner commenced the hotel in the year 2013 and was also issued with D&O license which was renewed for the year 2014-2015.
The petitioner had also been issued with a license under the Food Safety and Standards Act, which later was not renewed for reason of non renewal of D&O license.
In fact the petitioner had approached this Court with a writ petition seeking direction to the Food Safety Authority to consider his application for renewal.

Directions were also issued in W.P.(C)
No.15494 of 2017, by judgment dated & 15413/2017 09.05.2017.

To understand the dispute further,
a brief statement of facts is required and essential.

4. The petitioner is said to have obtained lease of the building from one Ashraf, who was permitted to so lease out the building on the basis of an agreement for sale entered into with the owner of the property, one Jessy Joseph.
The said Jessy Joseph is also said to have transferred the property to one Jose Thomas whose sister and Power of Attorney is impleaded as the additional 3rd respondent.
The entire issue arose on the complaint raised by the additional 2nd respondent on an issue totally unconnected with the aforesaid transactions.

The additional 2nd respondent is said to have taken food from the restaurant of the petitioner and developed some problems, based on which a complaint was raised before the Corporation to verify as to whether there was a license issued to the petitioner.
The petitioner contends that the 2nd respondent is, in fact, a relative of the 3rd respondent and that the complaint was one initiated at the behest of the 3rd respondent.
The learned Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent however stoutly denies the same.

entities.text: writ petition Vincent Mathew vs The Corporation Of Kochi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent could have taken up appropriate proceedings on that allegation and the complaint on the question of licence was in fact unnecessary.

6. In any event, on that complaint the Corporation initiated proceedings and it was found that there was a dispute with respect to the possession and ownership of the property; which alone is germane for consideration in the writ petition.
The Corporation had revoked the licence issued to the petitioner on such doubt raised as to the possession of the petitioner being not valid.
The dispute was also on the ground that Jessy Joseph had in fact transferred the property to Jose Thomas and hence without a consent of Jose Thomas there could be no issuance of a D & O licence.
7. The revocation made by the Secretary was challenged before the Council, which rejected the appeal.
The order in appeal was challenged before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions (Tribunal), which set aside the order at Ext.P3.

entities.text: Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions (Tribunal)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Tribunal found that not even a preliminary enquiry was conducted as to the ownership and possession of the property.
It was also found that the Appellate Authority has not assigned any reason to reject the appeal.
On the aforesaid findings the Tribunal remanded the issue to the Secretary for re-consideration afresh by Ext.P3 order.

It was & 15413/2017 specifically directed that the Secretary would look into whether Ashraf,
who is said to have given possession of the property to the petitioner had obtained possession of the building prior to the sale deed in favour of the 3rd respondent.
It was also observed that the findings in the Tribunal's order would not affect the right of the 3rd respondent to take appropriate legal remedy against the appeal through a competent Civil Court.
8. After Ext.P3, the additional respondents impleaded before the Tribunal, ie; the additional respondents 2 and 3 filed a review which was rejected as per Ext.P4.
The Secretary of the Corporation even after the remand did not make any consideration.
This led to the closure of the petitioner's restaurant on the basis of the interim order in the other writ petition.
As of now, it is admitted that the Corporation has not considered the issue and it is pending before the Secretary and is posted for hearing on 18.07.2017.
Considering the rival contentions raised as to the possession, this Court had called for the files of the Corporation.
It is found that Jessy Joseph on the very same day ie; on 23.09.2013 executed an agreement for sale in favour of Ashraf and also executed a sale deed in favour of Jose Thomas.

Three suits are said to be pending,
one filed by Ashraf, another filed by the petitioner and the third filed by Jose Joseph.
Ashraf's suit is one for specific performance and setting aside the sale deed.
The petitioner's suit is one for injunction, restraining the respondents from evicting the petitioner, unless in accordance with law.

Jose Thomas too filed a suit for recovery of possession; which makes it very evident that the possession is not with the said person, whose power of attorney is the additional 3rd & 15413/2017 respondent herein.

4 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has verified the files and found the agreement for sale as also the deed of sale.
There is also a consent issued by Jessy Joseph dated 21.11.2013.

The leaned Counsel, who appears for the additional respondents 2 and 3 submits that Jessy Joseph was not even in India, when the said consent was issued, ie: on 21.11.2013, which consent is found to be in a non judicial stamp paper.
That again is a matter to be adjudicated on facts by leading sufficient evidence, which exercise this Court will not embark upon in the present proceedings.

1.1. Apparently, what comes out from the above facts is that the petitioner was put in possession of the building from 2013 and Ashraf, who claims on the basis of the sale agreement, has no complaint against the petitioner continuing in occupation, though he is not made a party herein.

It is &
15413/2017 submitted by the petitioner that in the civil suit filed by Ashraf, he has admitted that the possession has been handed over validly by Ashraf to the petitioner, on the basis of the terms of the sale agreement.

As for Jose Thomas, who claims title over the property, he has filed a suit for recovery of possession, which makes it very clear that the possession is not with the said person,
though a sale deed has been executed on 23.09.2013.
The petitioner hence is found to be validly put in possession of the building at that point.
However, his continuance would definitely be subject to the result of the suit filed by the respective parties.
As of now, the petitioner's application for renewal of licence cannot be rejected only on the ground of there being no existing D&O licence going by the facts.
There cannot also be any insistence for a consent from the landlord.
The possession of the petitioner is valid and cannot now be interfered with.

The Secretary would &
15413/2017 consider the issue in accordance with the declaration made by this Court and pass orders on the renewal application on 18.07.2017 itself, on which date, the hearing is posted.
12. The respondents 2 and 3 or their authorised representatives shall also be present on 18.07.2017 at 11.00 A.M and so shall the petitioner or his authorised representative.
The Secretary shall consider the same in accordance with the directions herein above and pass appropriate orders.
On the basis of the same, the petitioner would be entitled to approach the Food Safety Authority also.
In the result W.P.(C) No.15413 of 2017 would stand disposed of with the above observations.
W.P.(C) No.13743 of 2017 would stand dismissed.
No costs.
